title: The Nearest Star Is a Cherry Past Cairo. How Do We Know?
description:
How Far Is the Nearest Star?
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=c5AdqQsnnys

Shrink the Sun to the size of a grapefruit: Earth is a pinhead fifteen metres away, and the nearest star, Proxima Centauri, is a cherry about four thousand kilometres away.

Sources: Gaia Collaboration, Vallenari et al. 2023 (A&A 674, A1), Proxima Centauri at 4.24 light-years (4.01 × 10^13 km) · Kervella, Thévenin & Lovis 2017 (A&A 598, L7), Proxima Centauri radius.

Pictures: ESO La Silla southern sky time-lapses and star fields (eso0905a, CC BY 4.0) and NASA Blue Marble Earth imagery, alongside AI-assisted voice and editing. Facts: every number is checked against the sources listed above.
Image credits: ESO; NASA.

social.hook: If the Sun were a grapefruit in London, the nearest star would be a cherry past Cairo.
social.question: Does shrinking the solar system make 4.24 light-years feel even bigger?
